references.text: The Gibeonites made peace with Israel and were made servants as hewers of wood and drawers of water, illustrating the principle that those who surrender are subjected to forced labor.
The Gibeonites were made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the entire congregation, an example of how peaceful surrender led to compulsory service.
Only Gibeon made peace with the Israelites, while all other cities were conquered by force, showing the contrast between peaceful surrender and war.
Solomon imposed forced labor on the remaining Canaanite peoples, a continuation of the practice described in Deuteronomy of making surrendered peoples into workers.
Issachar bent his shoulder to bear burdens and became a slave under forced labor, using the same Hebrew word 'mas' (forced labor).
The prophecy that nations which will not serve Israel shall perish relates to the theme of submission and service for those who seek peace.
